I will start from what has worked for me in Quzhou and then adjust a little for cost, water, and yield. On 7.5 mu, I cannot afford to gamble, but I also do not save fertilizer to the point that I lose production. My main land will stay in the wheat-maize system because that is still the most stable for my household, and with well irrigation I can push yield steadily if I feed the crop on time. I will keep a smaller piece for kohlrabi because cash flow from vegetables is useful, but I will not expand it too much because it needs more labor and tighter pest control than grain. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, and split nitrogen between base, jointing, and a small top-up if the stand looks weak. For maize after wheat, I will stay close to my usual hybrid practice, keep density steady, and feed more nitrogen than potassium because our grain response to nitrogen is still obvious, though I will not let potassium go too low. For kohlrabi, I will manage it more intensively because vegetable yield and quality drop fast if water or fertilizer is short. I do watch costs, but between wasting a little fertilizer and losing yield, I will spend the extra money on the main nutrients and keep pesticide use to the points when pressure is real.
